source.title: Robust Unlearnable Examples: Protecting Data Privacy Against Adversarial Learning
source.authors: Shaopeng Fu; Fengxiang He; Yang Liu; Li Shen; Da-Cheng Tao

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a complete paper, including appendices; it is not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the related question of whether unlearnable training data can still yield learned knowledge under adversarial training, but in image classifiers and data-protection noise rather than LLM unlearning.
record.gate_note: The study tests error-minimizing noise (EM) on image-classification data and reports test accuracy after adversarial training. These results bear on the broad recovery claim, but the attack is adversarial training—not the listed fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks—and the method is not an LLM unlearning method. Rows record EM results only; the paper's proposed REM method and its comparisons are not results on one of the named claim attacks.
record.test_reason: This paper studies 'unlearnable examples': imperceptible noise added to image training data so classifiers trained on it learn little. It does not study machine unlearning, meaning removing knowledge from an already-trained model, LLM or otherwise. Adversarial training on noise-protected CIFAR/ImageNet data is a different construct from recovering knowledge suppressed in an unlearned model. None of versions A–F is tested; the paper cites none of the claim's original sources. The word 'unlearnable' is a lexical coincidence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that error-minimizing noise fails under adversarial training because it cannot suppress the adversarial training loss. They propose robust error-minimizing noise (REM), generated via min-min-max optimization with EOT, which protects image data against adversarial training in most settings. Protection weakens at large adversarial radii, on DenseNet-121, and without EOT.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies image-data protection with error-minimizing and robust error-minimizing noise, not LLM unlearning. Its recovery test is adversarial training on protected training data.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies with adversarial training radius, dataset, and model architecture. The authors report weaker REM protection at larger adversarial radii and loss of REM protection when generated without EOT.

fits_no_version.finding: Error-minimizing noise on image training data loses its protection under adversarial training. ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 accuracy goes from 13.20% (ERM) to 88.62% at radius 4/255, versus 89.51% clean.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-poisoning protections ('unlearnable examples') for image classifiers are broken by adversarial training. This is a distinct phenomenon from shallow LLM unlearning.

record.problems: The evidence concerns image classifiers and poisoned training data, not LLM unlearning. Results are reported as point accuracies without uncertainty estimates in the supplied tables.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Proposed REM and comparisons against TAP/NTGA are not entered because adversarial training is not one of versions B–F and those methods are not the unlearning methods in the claim.

untested.parts: All: no unlearning method applied to a trained model; no LLMs.
All. REM resists adversarial training on poisoned data, which is not a robust unlearning method.

record.verdict_notes: The reader misread 'unlearnable examples' (data protection against training) as machine unlearning. The rows are internally accurate against Tables 1 and 3, but bear on no version of the shallow-unlearning claim. All rows used the invalid version id 'V1'. Recommend excluding this study from the phenomenon.

versions.untested_parts: Tests EM protection against adversarial training on image datasets. Does not test LLM unlearning methods, the listed simple attacks, or preservation of general ability in an unlearned LLM.
Fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
Activation-direction ablation or evidence about access-blocking versus deletion.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Resistance of a newer method to the attacks listed in the claim.

relation.reason: Different construct; no version is tested or used. The paper (2022) predates and does not cite the originals (WMDP 2024, WHP 2023). cites_only is the least-engagement option in the set.

tranche.reason: The paper studies protecting image training data with noise (unlearnable examples), not removing knowledge from a trained model. It neither tests nor uses any version of the claim.

source_check.notes: All 25 rows match Table 1 (EM column, ResNet-18) and Table 3 (EM column, rho_a=4/255). R5 and R17 are duplicates. Printed Table 3 RN-18 CIFAR-100 (63.43 clean / 64.17 EM) conflicts with Table 1 (64.50 / 63.43), so it is likely a typo in the paper. Study is off-topic: data poisoning, not machine unlearning.

statements.correction: Table 1, ResNet-18, CIFAR-10, EM noise rho_u=8/255: 13.20% at rho_a=0 (ERM), 88.62% at rho_a=4/255; clean data at 4/255 gives 89.51%. This is image-data poisoning, not unlearning of a trained model.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-subset EM data at adversarial training radii 1/255 through 4/255; CIFAR-10 at radii 3/255 and 4/255; and the model-architecture settings in Table 3
reader_labels.reason: EM-protected data that had very low accuracy under ERM reaches accuracy close to the clean-data reference under adversarial training (R4–R5, R7–R10, R12–R15, R16–R25). This is recovery in the tested vision setting, not a test of the claim's named LLM attacks.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 at adversarial training radii 1/255 and 2/255
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy increases markedly from the EM-only result but remains below the clean-data reference (R2–R3), so recovery is incomplete in these conditions.
